nodes.question: Is the source paper visibly stuffed inside the source cup in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the paper from the source image placed inside the cup from the source image, with visible evidence it has been stuffed into it. nodes.question: Is there visible progress toward putting the source paper into the source cup, based on edited objects that can be reliably matched to both source objects?

Unknown if either identity or the relevant placement cannot be established. Proximity, overlap, or a hand-held item near a round object alone does not establish a match or progress.
nodes.binding: Match the edited objects to the source paper and cup using visual and contextual evidence. program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

s2: The node’s conservative identity gate is appropriate: the edited frame shows a hand-held blue printed item and a reddish round object, not clearly the source paper and blue cup, so the trace’s unknown is supported by the images. Do not force `no` from the aggregate reference label; it is not atomic ground truth, and the rubric explicitly keeps insufficient evidence unresolved. The metric failure is unresolved coverage, not a transport or schema failure (the node executed validly, was queried, and returned valid uncertainty). For typed edits, investigate whether the binding/criteria can use stronger contextual and relational cues to distinguish identity from superficial color or shape, while retaining the requirement that both source objects be reliably matched before judging progress. Clarify how to assess visible partial progress when identity is supported despite appearance changes, and keep unknown when identity or placement genuinely cannot be established. The high-confidence unknown is not itself evidence of a bad decision; avoid lowering confidence or relaxing the evidence threshold merely to match this one reference.
s1: The node executed correctly; this is not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. The unresolved result is defensible: the source shows a white sheet and blue cup, while the edit shows a hand-held blue printed item beside a reddish round object, so neither identity nor the paper–cup relationship is established. Improve the binding/criteria to use contextual and relational cues across the source and edit—not color or shape alone—and explicitly distinguish a changed appearance from an unmatchable object. Assess visible partial progress only when the relevant source objects and their placement can be supported; retain unknown when identity or placement remains genuinely indeterminate. Do not force `no` from the aggregate reference label or lower confidence merely to improve coverage.
